response.summary: The revision fixes all twelve first-round findings, and F9 is accepted as clarified. The new step that moves the five opening units ahead of truth-validity, negation and contraposition adds two problems. First, it silently changes what existing stage assignments contain, because a stage assignment's unit list is recomputed from the course order every time it loads. Second, it leaves the later contraposition unit pointing to a "six-step process" that the opening no longer teaches. There are also smaller gaps: the direct Vite build skips the postbuild canonical check, and one route test that hard-codes a level label isn't in the plan's test-update list.

findings.evidence: A stage assignment stores only its starting `unitId`. `conditionalAssignmentUnitIds` rebuilds the unit list on every load with `getCurriculumUnits(conditionalUnits, target.unitId)`, which slices the current order. After the reorder: a stage row starting at truth-validity, negation or contraposition loses group-1 and group-2, and ActionGate will refuse those lessons that were reachable before. A stage row starting at group-1 or group-2 gains truth-validity, negation and contraposition. Course-scope students partway through contraposition will be sent back to group-1. That contradicts "Keep the 30 unit IDs and teacher assignments", and the plan doesn't mention it.
findings.fix: Before reordering, query existing `bootcamp_module` rows with `conditional_target.scope = 'stage'` or legacy `?start=` source IDs (read-only). Either confirm none are affected, or decide and record what happens to them: accept and tell the teacher, or map old start IDs to an equivalent new start. Add an assignments test that pins the expected `unitIds` for stages starting at group-1 and at contraposition after the reorder.

findings.evidence: The contraposition unit's teaching says "The six-step process finishes by translating back to English" and "Use the six steps to learn and check translation". Today those steps are introduced in group-1 and group-2, which come later. After the reorder, contraposition follows group-1 and group-2, and the revised opening carries no step count. So contraposition will refer to a process the student never saw, and treat "six steps" as canonical, which the plan rules out.
findings.fix: Bring the contraposition paragraphs into scope as a dependency of the reorder, which the 'unrelated curriculum' boundary shouldn't block. Reword them to build on the opening's diagram routine (indicator, readable ideas, side rule, English readback) without a step count, or accept and document the dangling reference. Grep all units that now follow the opening for 'six' and for references to earlier units that have moved.

findings.evidence: Calling `node node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js build` directly avoids prebuild, but it also skips `postbuild` (`verify-no-canonical-in-build.mjs`) and the explanations-manifest step. The build proof would then omit the repository's own check that no canonical content ships in the bundle.
findings.fix: After the direct build, run `npm run verify:no-canonical` explicitly and report the result. Also say whether skipping `build-explanations-manifest.mjs` matters for the conditional bundle.

findings.evidence: The routes test finds the group-2 guided-activity link by the name `/Next action: Level 3 skill drill/`. The plan removes student-facing level labels around lessons, and group-2 is an opening unit, so this test will fail. The plan's test-update list names only the opening render tests in ConditionalLessonNote.test.tsx.
findings.fix: Add routes.test.tsx:83 to the planned test updates. Assert the new link text, and keep the href assertions for `level=advanced`, `unit=group-2` and `assignment=skill` so assigned-difficulty logic is still covered.

findings.evidence: The plan says the preview is DEV-only but doesn't say how it's kept out of production: a guard on `import.meta.env.DEV`, a separate HTML entry not listed in the Vite inputs, or a dev-server-only route. A route registered without the guard would ship an unauthenticated lesson renderer in the production bundle.
findings.fix: Name the mechanism, and add a check after the build (for example, grep `dist/` for the preview entry or its route path) showing it isn't in the production output.

coverage: Re-read the amended plan text and host dispositions and checked them against first-round findings F1-F12. All are addressed in the plan; F9 is accepted as clarified.
Read scripts/conditionals/import-content.ts: the generator writes only curriculum.generated.json, from foundations.source.ts plus applications.source.ts in array order.
Traced how stage assignments resolve: conditionalBootcampAssignment.ts:40-49 (stores only the start unitId) → assignments.ts:44-46 → curriculumPath.ts:42-46 (slices the current order).
Searched the conditional test files for unit-order and level-label dependencies (routes.test.tsx, assignments.test.ts, progress.test.ts, ConditionalLessonNote.test.tsx).
Searched the content sources for 'six-step', 'six steps' and '6 step' references.
Re-checked package.json build, prebuild and postbuild scripts against the new direct-Vite build approach.
limitations: This is a review of the amended plan only. No implementation diff was inspected, and I made no claim about typecheck, tests, build or rendering.
I couldn't query the Supabase assignment rows, so I can't tell whether any live stage assignments are affected by the reorder.
I didn't re-read the corrected primary draft to confirm the must-attend fix; I relied on the host's statement.
I didn't inspect the Vite config, the remaining content in applications.source.ts, Intro to LR source, voice and copy references, or NotebookLM outputs.
